6.5a — Platforming Studio: The Gauntlet

Build day. Every skill from this unit — jump, ground check, feel mercies, double jump — goes into ONE room that a partner must survive blind. The grade is the room's clarity: a stranger should finish it with no instructions from you.

Studio Brief ~40 min

The contract:

  • One connected room (tilemap is fine, flat platforms are fine — polish is NOT the point)
  • Five sections, each testing one thing: (1) basic jump gap, (2) height — a jump UP two tiles, (3) a spike floor crossed by small platforms (2.2a spikes), (4) a soft gate — visible coin unreachable without the boots (6.4a), and (5) a turret on a ledge (3.1a) you pass UNDER, not over
  • Start pad and end flag (a trigger that prints "GAUNTLET CLEAR" — full scenes come in Unit 7)
  • Deaths must respawn at START (you know the loop)

Rules of the studio:

  • You may NOT explain the room verbally. Ever. The room teaches by layout.
  • Every section must be passable two ways or with two timing windows — no pixel-perfect single solutions.
  • Keep a notes file open: every "hmm" from a tester is a bug you have not coded yet.

Build order that works: floor and walls first → start flag → section by section, TEST EACH ALONE with a temporary teleport → then chain them → mercies LAST (6.3a numbers after the shapes are real). Teams that tune feel first end up tuning air.

Bug Hunt: Design bugs (they count)

  1. A tester dies at your spike gap 4+ times in a row. That is not a hard jump — it is a READING bug. What did the room fail to say, and what geometry (not text!) fixes it?
  2. A tester grabs the boots and backtracks — past your soft gate to the coin. Wait: did they find the gate, or did they find NOTHING? What visual did you forget?
  3. A tester walks past the end trigger without noticing. Why is "print to console" not enough — and what is the cheapest visible response?
Playtest ~15 min

Silent-watching rules from 2.4a apply, but today record NUMBERS per section (this habit becomes the dataset unit in 9.5a):

SectionDeathsTime (sec)Tester said…
1 — gap
2 — height
3 — spikes
4 — gate
5 — turret

Tinker: Iterate with numbers

  1. Any section with deaths ≥ 3 across two testers gets ONE change (not five). Which change did the notes point to — and why is "make it easier" almost never the right change?
  2. Swap rooms with another team. Play THEIR gauntlet, then say one sentence of admiration and one of cruelty. Both must be about geometry, not effort.
  3. Commit + push: "6.5a: gauntlet v1 + playtest notes".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Ship a five-section gauntlet that a stranger finishes blind
  • Explain every section as a test of a specific unit skill
  • Collect death/time data instead of vibes
  • Make ONE numbered change per playtest round and re-test
